clue.text: Part of body at swinging club

parts.note: swinging, in the sixties slang sense of fashionable and lively, means hip
a joint is informal for a club or bar where people gather

explanation.surface: Something about a body part at a lively club, as if a dancer had hurt themselves on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging club' looks like a golf club or cosh being swung; instead 'swinging' is the trendy sense and 'club' is a nightspot.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball-and-socket connection between pelvis and thigh bone is an anatomical part.

clue.text: I had, with eastern science, visionary speculation

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
an ology is an informal word for any branch of science or learning

explanation.surface: Someone combines their own learning with Eastern science into a grand visionary theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of ideas can be dismissed as abstract, visionary theorising, an older sense of the word.

clue.text: Those less advanced are taught here

definitions.text: Those less advanced are taught here

parts.words: Those less advanced are taught here
parts.note: reads like a remedial class for slow learners, but the less advanced are simply the younger pupils, who are taught at the stage before senior level

explanation.definitionFit: A school for younger children teaches pupils not yet advanced in age or grade.

clue.text: Is taking award to one on a Mediterranean island

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who has won an award heads off to a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, an order awarded by the British monarch; 'taking', 'to' and 'on' just string the pieces together in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcanic island in the Bay of Naples, off southern Italy, lies in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Square mat used for basket

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can stand for square
a rug is a small floor mat

explanation.surface: A square mat is repurposed as a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: A trug is a shallow, oblong garden basket, a word mostly heard in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow wooden basket used by gardeners to carry flowers and produce.

clue.text: Something sticky to read in aeroplane?

definitions.text: Something sticky to read in aeroplane?

parts.words: Something sticky to read in aeroplane?
parts.note: reads as an in-flight magazine, a paper for those who fly, while really it is the sticky sheet that traps insects

explanation.definitionFit: Sticky sheets hung up to catch insects carry a name that sounds like airline reading matter.

clue.text: Non-clerical individual getting into resin

indicators.note: getting into means the single letter goes inside the word for resin

parts.note: lac is a resinous substance secreted by insects, used to make shellac
I, the numeral one, stands for a single individual

explanation.surface: An ordinary person, not a priest, gets caught up in sticky resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay, as opposed to clergy, is the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Slogan's rewritten before time of openness

indicators.note: rewritten tells us the letters of the slogan are set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: A political slogan gets reworded to herald an era of openness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slogan's' looks like a possessive but gives all seven letters; 'before' only places the time piece after the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian term for the policy of transparency under Gorbachev in the late Soviet era.

clue.text: Absentees cannot give their names in it

definitions.text: Absentees cannot give their names in it

parts.words: Absentees cannot give their names in it
parts.note: a register read aloud asks each person to answer to their name, which those not there obviously cannot do

explanation.definitionFit: A roll call is the reading out of a list of names to check attendance.

clue.text: Some who move inside have distinctive manner

indicators.note: some of means only part of the words move inside is used

explanation.surface: Those who move in have a distinctive style.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein can mean a particular style or mood, as in writing in a humorous vein.

clue.text: Among people of influence in the Andes perhaps

explanation.surface: Somewhere among the powerful, or else up in the South American mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means among powerful people, while literally it describes being up at altitude, as in a lofty mountain range.

clue.text: Lady's about to ingest large number of fast particles, they fall in spring

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Lady's about to ingest large number of fast particles, they fall in spring (5,7)', solution APRIL SHOWERS. 'Lady' gives APRIL and 'they fall in spring' defines, but no parse accounts for 'about to ingest large number of fast particles' giving SHOWERS; a clue-database search confirms the text but not the wordplay.
annotationWithheld.clue: Lady's about to ingest large number of fast particles, they fall in spring

clue.text: Arab to come down by heath

parts.note: a Moor is a North African of Arab and Berber descent
to land is to come down to earth from the air

explanation.surface: An Arab arrives by air beside the heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Open uncultivated upland covered with heather is heath country.

clue.text: Produce reluctantly when excavation has finished

parts.note: an archaeological dig is an excavation
up can mean finished or over, as in time is up

explanation.surface: Something is reluctantly brought forward once the archaeological excavation is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something, such as old facts, is to bring it out with effort.

clue.text: By proxy according to expert

parts.note: per means according to, as in per instructions
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: An expert advises acting by proxy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, abbreviated pp, is used when signing a letter on another person's behalf.

clue.text: Seychelles and north Carolina have agreement in time

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle registration code for the Seychelles
NC is the US postal abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: An island nation and an American state reach a timely accord.
explanation.definitionFit: Being synchronised means things happen together at the same moment.

clue.text: Became a sitting tenant?

parts.note: sounds like gaining the legal right to stay in a rented home, but read literally it is crouching down, or occupying a property without permission

explanation.definitionFit: Occupying an empty building without permission, or simply crouching on one's haunches, fits both senses.

clue.text: Tease us going back for sweetener

indicators.note: going back means the letters of tease and us are written in reverse order

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Teasing us in return for a sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns the whole run RAGUS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucrose and its relatives are the classic substance used to sweeten food and drink.

clue.text: Deliberately cruel first when acid's spilt outside

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters sit around the word for first
spilt suggests the acid is splashed about, scattering its letters

parts.note: 1st, written IST, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: A deliberately cruel act comes first when acid is spilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks like an adverb of order but is written 1ST, read as the letters I, S, T; 'acid's' gives five letters, the 's counting.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking pleasure in inflicting pain describes deliberate cruelty.

clue.text: Lean over the table

explanation.surface: An instruction to lean across the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that tilts to one side is said to do this; a catalogue or tabulated record is also called this.

clue.text: Startle ram inside damaging plant

indicators.note: inside means the scrambled letters go within the word for startle

parts.note: to shock is to startle

indicators.note: damaging suggests the ram's letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A startled ram, trapped inside, damages a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaging plant' reads as a harmful weed; 'damaging' is the scramble signal for the animal, and the plant is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-leaved clover, the emblem of Ireland, is a plant.

clue.text: Defend keep in higher position previously

indicators.note: previously means the piece for higher position comes before the word for keep

parts.note: up means in a higher position
to hold is to keep

explanation.surface: Defend the keep, the castle tower, from a higher position as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' suggests a castle tower to defend, but it is just the verb hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or maintain a decision or principle against challenge is to defend it.

clue.text: Top of the jetty?

parts.note: reads like the uppermost part, but the top is the far end of a seaside landing stage

explanation.definitionFit: The seaward end of a jetty or seaside walkway is named this way.

clue.text: Insect found somewhere near wigtown

indicators.note: found somewhere in means the letters lie within the words near wigtown

explanation.surface: An insect turns up somewhere near a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'nEAR WIGtown'; Wigtown is a small town in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature with pincers at its tail end, common in gardens, is an insect.

clue.text: Back-breaking limit

parts.note: recalls the proverb about the final light item loaded onto a camel that breaks its back

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the final small burden that makes something unbearable.

clue.text: Half-continental wallaroo

explanation.surface: A wallaroo that is half continental.
explanation.walkthrough: Continental here means European, of the European mainland; its first half supplies the first sense. A wallaroo is a sturdy kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: The first half of European works as a prefix for the continent; it is also the name of a large Australian kangaroo species, the common wallaroo.

clue.text: Token gesture

explanation.surface: A token gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a mark or indication and a movement of the hand conveying meaning share this word.

clue.text: Energy at present enough in the past

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
now means at present

explanation.surface: Energy now was enough back then.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning sufficient, so it is enough as used in older English.

clue.text: Coating

parts.note: reads as putting on a layer of paint, but it also means dressing someone in a coat or robe

explanation.definitionFit: Dressing in a robe is putting a garment on, a covering layer.

clue.text: Again ask eccentric for port

indicators.note: eccentric suggests something odd and irregular, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking again at the port is thought eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese city on Kyushu is a major seaport.
